experiment: FL-IDS Privacy Stack Evaluation — pure_he profile

dataset.preprocessing: Full corpus loaded, DDoS_TCP capped to 18% of total (VARS-FL methodology), stratified subsample to max_rows preserving per-class proportions

homomorphic_encryption.note: All classifier params routed through HE; server never sees plaintext model weights

runs.server_aggregation: Homomorphic aggregation of sensitive (HE) layers, plaintext FedAvg of bulk layers (0 params in this full-coverage config); round completed server-side in 0.16-0.19s

runs.run_label: throttled — simulated constrained IoT gateway (0.5 vCPU)

analysis.cpu_throttling_effect: Halving vCPU allocation (1.0 -> 0.5) produced an approx 2x increase in per-round training time for both clients (client_0: ~40s -> ~81s; client_1: ~27s -> ~54s), consistent with training being CPU-bound and scaling near-linearly with available compute.
analysis.he_overhead_under_throttling: HE encryption time roughly doubled in absolute terms (0.30-0.35s -> 0.63-0.70s) alongside the compute halving, but remained a small fraction (<1%) of total round time in both configurations. This supports the conclusion that CKKS encryption overhead does not become the bottleneck as device compute shrinks -- training dominates at every tested compute level.
analysis.memory_stability: Peak RAM stayed within 321-333MB across BOTH unthrottled and throttled runs, i.e. memory footprint appears CPU-independent for this model size. A 400MB mem_limit holds with a consistent ~70-90MB safety margin under both conditions.
analysis.non_iid_effect: Client 0's larger partition (38,440 vs 23,294 samples) consistently trains slower than client 1 across all runs, tracking partition size rather than indicating any bug -- expected outcome of Dirichlet(alpha=0.7) non-IID partitioning.

real_time_iot_projection.disclaimer: Extrapolated from measured Docker cpus= throttling on host x86 hardware. Real ARM-based gateway performance will differ due to instruction set, cache size, NEON/SIMD availability, and thermal throttling on passively-cooled devices. Treat as order-of-magnitude estimates pending real hardware validation.

measured_anchor_points.half_core_simulated: 54-82s/round (measured; roughly comparable to a Raspberry Pi 4-class Cortex-A72 gateway with one core reserved for OS/networking)

projected_untested.quarter_core_simulated: Estimated ~2-3 min/round (not yet measured; recommend running cpus=0.25 for empirical confirmation)
projected_untested.sub_1ghz_cortex_a53_class_gateway: Estimated several minutes/round; would require real hardware or further throttled simulation to confirm

real_time_iot_projection.recommended_next_step: Run identical experiment with cpus=0.25 on both clients to obtain a third empirical anchor point, enabling a measured (not purely extrapolated) compute-vs-round-time scaling curve for the paper.
